role: TCA cycle intermediate that links carbon and nitrogen metabolism through transamination.
biochem: 2-oxoglutarate is a key intermediate of the tricarboxylic acid (TCA) cycle. 2-Oxoglutarate is produced from isocitrate and it is converted into succinyl-CoA. It also participates in the glutamate metabolism.
relevance_diet: 2-oxoglutarate concentrations were significantly influenced by feeding systems (p < 0.001), being in higher concentrations in milk from PMR diets compared to GRS and TMR diets.
relevance_season: 2-Oxoglutarate did not differ significantly across seasons (p = 0.143).

role: Main circulating ketone body. The mammary gland uses it for fat synthesis; raised levels point to negative energy balance.
biochem: 3-hydroxybutyrate is produced in the liver from acetyl-CoA during periods of high energy demands such as early lactation.
relevance_diet: 3-hydroxybutyrate concentrations were significantly influenced by feeding systems (p < 0.001), with higher concentrations in milk from TMR diets compared to GRS and PMR diets.
relevance_season: 3-hydroxybutyrate concentrations were significantly influenced by season (p = 0.003), with the highest concentrations observed in winter and lower concentrations detected during spring, summer, and autumn.

chem_class: Short-chain volatile fatty acid (VFA) belonging to the organic acid class
role: Short-chain fatty acid from rumen fermentation and the main carbon source for de novo milk fat synthesis.
biochem: Acetate is produced by microbial fermentation of carbohydrates in the rumen and is the major VFA absorbed by ruminants.
relevance_diet: Acetate concentrations did not differ significantly across the different feeding systems (GRS, PMR, TMR) (p = 0.059).
relevance_season: Acetate concentrations were significantly influenced by season (p = 0.006), with lower concentrations in spring and summer and higher in winter and autumn.

role: Ketone body produced by the liver when body fat is mobilised, typically in early lactation.
biochem: Acetoacetate is produced from butyrate metabolism in the rumen epithelium and from hepatic ketogenesis during negative energy balance periods.
relevance_season: Acetoacetate concentrations were significantly influenced by season (p < 0.001), with concentrations decreasing progressively from winter to autumn.

role: Ketone body formed from acetoacetate; milk acetone is used when screening herds for ketosis.
biochem: Formed through decarboxylation of acetoacetate, process that occurs during negative energy balance when glucose availability is limited, leading to lipid mobilization.
relevance_diet: Acetone concentrations varied significantly by diet (p < 0.001). The highest concentrations were found in the PMR group, whereas the GRS group had the lowest concentrations.
relevance_season: Acetone concentrations were significantly influenced by season (p < 0.001), with the highest concentrations in winter and the lowest in summer.

chem_class: Non-essential amino acid belong to the group of nitrogenous compounds
role: Glucogenic amino acid taken up from blood; also a building block of milk proteins.
biochem: Alanine is synthesized in the muscle tissue by transamination of pyruvate and plays a key role in the amino sugar metabolism.
relevance_diet: Alanine concentrations were significantly influenced by feeding system (p < 0.001), with PMR and TMR diets having higher concentrations than GRS diets. In the partial least squares discriminant analysis (PLS-DA), alanine exhibited a variable importance in projection (VIP) score higher than 1.0, with elevated concentrations associated with PMR diets.
relevance_season: Alanine concentrations were significantly influenced by season (p = 0.030), decreasing slightly from winter to autumn.

role: Amino acid that links the TCA cycle with nitrogen metabolism.
biochem: Aspartate has an important role in the nitrogen metabolism, participating in the urea cycle.
relevance_diet: Aspartate concentrations are not significantly affected by feeding system (p = 0.07).

chem_class: Quaternary ammonium compound belong to organic nitrogen compounds
role: Methyl donor formed by oxidising choline; also an osmolyte found in some feeds such as beet.
biochem: Betaine is derived from choline metabolism and functions as a methyl group donor. It is also involved in osmoregulation, protecting cells against osmotic stress.
relevance_diet: Betaine concentrations were significantly influenced by feeding system (p < 0.001), with higher concentrations in milk from PMR group, followed by TMR, and with GRS having the lowest concentrations.
relevance_season: Betaine concentrations were significantly influenced by season (p < 0.001), with higher concentrations in winter and autumn and lower in spring and summer.

role: Short-chain fatty acid; free butyrate in milk can come from rumen-derived precursors and from lipolysis of milk fat.
biochem: Butyrate is one of the major microbial fermentation end-products in the rumen through microbial fermentation of dietary carbohydrates and fibres.
relevance_diet: Butyrate concentrations were significantly influenced by feeding system (p < 0.001), with higher concentrations in milk from PMR group compared to GRS and TMR.
relevance_season: Butyrate did not differ significantly between seasons (p = 0.105).

role: Medium-chain fatty acids made de novo in the mammary gland; free forms rise when milk fat is broken down.
biochem: Caprate and caprylate are synthesised in the mammary gland and can also come from the diet. Caprate and caprylate provide an energy source for newborns.
relevance_diet: Caprate and caprylate concentrations were significantly influenced by feeding system (p < 0.001), with higher concentrations in milk from PMR diets compared to GRS and TMR diets.
relevance_season: Caprate and caprylate concentrations were significantly influenced by season (p = 0.002), with lower concentrations in spring, intermediate in summer, and higher in winter and autumn.
note: Caprate and caprylate were quantified together because their signals in the spectrum are very similar and tend to overlap, making it difficult to distinguish them accurately.

role: Carries long-chain fatty acids into mitochondria so they can be oxidised for energy.
biochem: Carnitine plays a critical role in mitochondrial energy metabolism by transporting long-chain fatty acids across the mitochondrial membrane for β-oxidation.
relevance_diet: Carnitine concentrations were significantly influenced by the feeding system (p < 0.001). In spring, concentrations were similar across the three diets. In summer, they were highest in milk from TMR diets, followed by PMR and GRS diets. In autumn, the highest concentrations were observed in GRS diets, followed by TMR, while PMR diets resulted in the lowest concentrations.
relevance_season: Carnitine concentrations were significantly influenced by season (p < 0.001), with lower concentrations in spring and summer and higher in winter and autumn.

role: Essential nutrient and precursor of phosphatidylcholine; milk carries it mostly as phosphocholine and glycerophosphocholine.
biochem: Choline is involved in the phospholipid synthesis, acetylcholine production, and methyl-group transfer. Choline plays an important role in lipid transport and cell membrane integrity.
relevance_diet: Choline concentrations were significantly influenced by feeding system (p < 0.001), with higher concentrations in GRS diets, followed by TMR and with the lowest concentrations in PMR diets.
relevance_season: Choline concentrations were significantly influenced by season (p < 0.001), with lower concentrations in winter and spring compared to summer and autumn.

role: Major organic acid of milk, made in the mammary gland and tied to de novo fat synthesis; proposed as an energy-balance indicator.
biochem: Citrate is an intermediate of the tricarboxylic acid (TCA) cycle. Citrate plays an important role in fatty acid synthesis and calcium regulation in milk. Citrate concentrations in milk reflect the balance between synthesis and milk secretion.
relevance_diet: Citrate concentrations were significantly influenced by feeding system (p < 0.001), with higher concentrations in the PMR diets in spring and summer and higher concentrations in GRS in autumn.
relevance_season: Citrate concentrations were significantly influenced by season (p < 0.001), with higher concentrations in winter and lower in spring, summer and autumn.

role: TCA cycle intermediate between citrate and isocitrate.
biochem: Cis-aconitate is an intermediate in the tricarboxylic acid (TCA) cycle, formed from citrate and converted to isocitrate.
relevance_diet: Cis-aconitate concentrations were significantly influenced by feeding systems (p < 0.001), with milk from PMR diets having higher concentrations compared to TMR, and with GRS having the lowest concentrations.

chem_class: Guanidine compound belong to nitrogenous organic acids
role: Energy buffer: it stores high-energy phosphate as creatine phosphate.
biochem: Creatine is synthesized in the liver and kidneys. Creatine plays a critical role in facilitating rapid generation of ATP during high energy demand.
relevance_diet: Creatine concentrations were significantly influenced by feeding system (p < 0.001), with higher concentrations in PMR diets, followed by TMR diets and with GRS diets with the lowest values.
relevance_season: Creatine did not differ significantly between seasons (p = 0.063).

chem_class: Phosphorylated guanidine compound belong to nitrogenous organic acids
role: High-energy phosphate store that regenerates ATP quickly.
biochem: Creatine phosphate acts as a phosphate donor to generate ATP during periods of intense energy demands.
relevance_diet: Creatine phosphate concentrations were significantly influenced by feeding system (p < 0.001), with milk from TMR diets having the highest concentrations, followed by PMR, and with GRS diets having the lowest concentrations. In the partial least squares discriminant analysis (PLS-DA), creatine phosphate exhibited a variable importance in projection (VIP) score higher than 1.0, with elevated concentrations associated with TMR diets.

role: Breakdown product of creatine phosphate that reflects muscle turnover.
biochem: Creatinine is formed from creatine in the muscle tissue and it is associated with negative energy balance (NEB).
relevance_diet: Creatinine concentrations were significantly influenced by feeding system (p < 0.001), with higher concentrations in milk from PMR diets compared to GRS and TMR in spring and summer, and with similar concentrations in autumn.
relevance_season: Creatinine concentrations were influenced by season (p < 0.001), decreasing significantly from winter to summer and autumn.

chem_class: Organosulfur compound belong to the sulfone chemical class
role: Sulfur compound from feed and microbial metabolism; its milk level is often linked to diet.
biochem: Dimethyl sulfone is associated with anti-inflammatory and antioxidant properties.
relevance_diet: Dimethyl sulfone concentrations were significantly influenced by feeding system (p < 0.001), with higher concentrations in milk from GRS diets compared to PMR and TMR diets in spring and summer and higher concentrations in milk from TMR diets in autumn. In the partial least squares discriminant analysis (PLS-DA), dimethyl sulfone exhibited a variable importance in projection (VIP) score higher than 1.0, with elevated concentrations associated with GRS diets.
relevance_season: Dimethyl sulfone concentrations were significantly influenced by season (p < 0.001), increasing from winter to summer and decreasing again in autumn.

chem_class: Aliphatic amine belonging to nitrogenous compounds
role: Amine produced when microbes break down choline and related compounds.
biochem: Dimethylamine arises from the microbial degradation of choline in the rumen.
relevance_diet: Dimethylamine concentrations were significantly influenced by feeding system (p = 0.004), with higher concentrations in milk from PMR diets compared to GRS and TMR.

role: Head group of phosphatidylethanolamine, a membrane phospholipid.
biochem: Component of membrane phospholipids. Ethanolamine is derived from serine and contributes to the synthesis of phosphatidylethanolamine.
relevance_diet: Ethanolamine concentrations were not significantly influenced by feeding systems (p = 0.09).

role: One-carbon unit produced during rumen fermentation.
biochem: Formate is produced during microbial fermentation in the rumen and serves as electron carrier. Methanogens and homoacetogens use formate as a source of electrons. 5
relevance_diet: Formate concentrations were significantly influenced by feeding systems (p < 0.001), with higher concentrations in milk from GRS and PMR diets compared to TMR. In the partial least squares discriminant analysis (PLS-DA), formate exhibited a variable importance in projection (VIP) score higher than 1.5, with elevated concentrations associated with PMR diets.
relevance_season: Formate did not show significant seasonal variation (p = 0.071).

role: Deoxy sugar found in milk oligosaccharides and glycoproteins.
biochem: Fucose is a component of glycoproteins and glycolipids. Fucosylated oligosaccharides contribute to the bioactivity of milk, especially the immune properties.
relevance_diet: Fucose concentrations were significantly influenced by feeding systems (p = 0.027), with higher concentrations in PMR diets overall.
relevance_season: Fucose concentrations were significantly influenced by season (p < 0.001), with lower concentrations in summer compared with the other seasons.

role: TCA cycle intermediate.
biochem: Fumarate is converted to malate in the tricarboxylic acid (TCA) cycle. Fumarate is crucial for cellular respiration and energy production.
relevance_diet: Fumarate concentrations were significantly influenced by feeding systems (p < 0.001), with higher concentrations in milk from PMR diets, followed by TMR diets and with GRS diets having the lowest concentrations.
relevance_season: Fumarate concentrations were significantly influenced by season (p = 0.040), with the highest concentrations observed in winter, followed by a slight decrease throughout the remainder of the year.

role: Monosaccharide that forms half of each lactose molecule.
biochem: Key component of the disaccharide lactose.
relevance_diet: Galactose concentrations were not significantly influenced by feeding systems (p = 0.903).

role: Lactose precursor; in ruminants it comes mostly from liver gluconeogenesis.
biochem: Glucose is the primary energy substrate for mammalians and precursor for lactose synthesis in the mammary gland.
relevance_diet: Glucose concentrations were significantly influenced by feeding systems (p < 0.001), with milk from PMR diets having higher concentrations than GRS and TMR.

role: Intermediate on the route from glucose to UDP-galactose and lactose.
biochem: Glucose-1-phosphate is produced during glycogenolysis and serves as substrate for UDP-glucose.
relevance_diet: Glucose-1-phosphate concentrations were significantly influenced by feeding system (p < 0.001), with higher concentrations in milk from TMR diets compared to PMR, and with GRS diets having the lowest concentrations. In the partial least squares discriminant analysis (PLS-DA), glucose-1-phosphate exhibited a variable importance in projection (VIP) score higher than 1.0, with elevated concentrations associated with TMR diets.
relevance_season: Glucose-1-phosphate concentrations were significantly influenced by season (p < 0.001), with higher concentrations observed in winter and lower concentrations during summer and autumn.

role: One of the most abundant free amino acids in milk.
biochem: Glutamate is formed through transamination, linking the TCA cycle and the urea cycle.
relevance_season: Glutamate concentrations were significantly influenced by season (p < 0.001), decreasing gradually from winter to autumn.

role: Glycine conjugate of benzoic acid derived from plant phenolics, so it tends to be higher on fresh forage.
biochem: Hippurate is conjugate of benzoic acid and glycine. Hippurate originates from microbial degradation of dietary aromatic compounds such as chlorogenic and caffeoylquinic acids found in fresh forage.
relevance_diet: Hippurate was the most distinctive metabolite identified in relation to dietary regimen, showing a strong proportional response to the amount of pasture in the cow's diet. Hippurate concentrations were significantly influenced by feeding systems (p < 0.001), with higher concentrations in milk from GRS diets, followed by PMR, and with TMR diets with the lowest concentrations. In the partial least squares discriminant analysis (PLS-DA), hippurate exhibited a variable importance in projection (VIP) score higher than 2.5 and in the biomarker analysis comparing GRS vs. TMR, it had an area under the curve (AUC) of 1.0, indicating excellent discriminatory power.
relevance_season: Hippurate concentrations were significantly influenced by season (p < 0.001), with higher concentrations in spring and summer and lower in winter and autumn.

role: Branched-chain fatty acid formed when rumen microbes ferment valine.
biochem: Isobutyrate is produced via microbial fermentation in the rumen.
relevance_diet: Isobutyrate concentrations were significantly influenced by feeding systems (p < 0.001), with milk from TMR diets having higher concentrations, followed by PMR, and with GRS diets having the lowest concentrations. In the partial least squares discriminant analysis (PLS-DA), isobutyrate exhibited a variable importance in projection (VIP) score higher than 2.0 and in the biomarker analysis comparing GRS vs. TMR, it had an area under the curve (AUC) of 0.90, indicating excellent discriminatory power.

role: Branched-chain essential amino acid.
biochem: Isoleucine is critical for casein synthesis and reflects the amino acid metabolism.
relevance_season: Isoleucine concentrations were significantly influenced by season (p = 0.003), with higher concentrations in winter and slightly lower in the remaining seasons.

role: End product of anaerobic glycolysis; bacterial activity in milk can also raise it.
biochem: Lactate is a product of anaerobic glycolysis formed from pyruvate under anaerobic conditions. 7
relevance_diet: Lactate concentrations were significantly influenced by feeding systems (p < 0.001), with milk from PMR diets having the highest concentrations, followed by TMR diets and with GRS diets having the lowest concentrations. In the partial least squares discriminant analysis (PLS-DA), lactate exhibited a variable importance in projection (VIP) score higher than 1.5, with elevated concentrations associated with PMR diets.
relevance_season: Lactate concentrations were significantly influenced by season (p < 0.001), with lower concentrations in spring and summer and higher in winter and autumn.

role: Main milk sugar; it draws water into milk and so largely sets milk volume.
biochem: Lactose is the principal carbohydrate in milk. Lactose is synthesized in the mammary gland and is composed of glucose and galactose.
relevance_diet: Lactose concentrations were not significantly influenced by feeding systems (p = 0.109).
relevance_season: Lactose concentrations were significantly influenced by season (p = 0.013), decreasing progressively from winter to autumn.

role: Branched-chain essential amino acid and a signal for protein synthesis.
biochem: Leucine plays a key role in protein synthesis. Leucine provides energy and intermediates for the tricarboxylic acid (TCA) cycle.
relevance_diet: Leucine concentrations were significantly influenced by feeding systems (p = 0.002), with higher concentrations in PMR and TMR diets compared to GRS diets.

role: TCA cycle intermediate.
biochem: Malate is an intermediate in the tricarboxylic acid (TCA) cycle. Malate is generated from fumarate and plays an important role in cellular respiration and energy production.
relevance_diet: Malate concentrations were significantly influenced by feeding system (p < 0.001), with higher concentrations in milk from PMR diets compared to GRS and TMR diets.

role: Dicarboxylic acid related to malonyl-CoA, the building block of fatty acid synthesis.
biochem: Malonate presence in milk reflects changes in mitochondrial energy metabolism and can be in higher concentrations in periods of metabolic stress
relevance_season: Malonate concentrations were significantly influenced by season (p < 0.001), with higher concentrations in winter and autumn and lower in spring and summer.

role: Released when microbes degrade pectin in forage.
biochem: Methanol is produced through microbial fermentation of pectins in the rumen. Methanol is typically metabolized to formaldehyde and then to formate.
relevance_diet: Methanol concentrations were significantly influenced by feeding systems (p < 0.001), with milk from TMR diets having the highest concentrations, followed by PMR diets, and with GRS diets having the lowest concentrations. In the partial least squares discriminant analysis (PLS-DA), methanol exhibited a variable importance in projection (VIP) score higher than 1.5, with elevated concentrations associated with TMR diets.

role: Amino sugar of milk oligosaccharides and glycoproteins; tends to be higher in early-lactation milk.
biochem: N-Acetylglucosamine serves as a precursor and a structural component of N-glycans. In milk, these N-glycans contribute to immune protection.
relevance_season: N-Acetylglucosamine concentrations were significantly influenced by season (p < 0.001), decreasing progressively from winter to autumn.

role: Acetyl ester of carnitine that reflects fatty acid oxidation and acetyl-CoA turnover.
biochem: O-acetylcarnitine is formed by the acetylation of carnitine within the mitochondria and helps buffering excess of acetyl groups. In milk, O-acetylcarnitine is associated with antioxidant and anti-inflammatory properties.
relevance_diet: O-Acetylcarnitine concentrations were significantly influenced by feeding systems (p < 0.001), with higher concentrations in milk from GRS and PMR diets compared to TMR diets.
relevance_season: O-Acetylcarnitine concentrations were significantly influenced by season (p < 0.001), with concentrations decreasing from winter to summer and increasing slightly again in autumn.

role: One of the main forms in which milk carries choline.
biochem: O-phosphocholine is involved in the metabolism and turnover of membrane phospholipids in the milk fat globule membrane.
relevance_season: O-phosphocholine concentrations were significantly influenced by season (p < 0.001), with concentrations decreasing drastically from winter to autumn.

role: Precursor of pyrimidine nucleotides and characteristically abundant in ruminant milk.
biochem: Orotic acid is a precursor of uridine monophosphate (UMP), essential for RNA and DNA synthesis.
relevance_diet: Orotic acid concentrations were not significantly influenced by feeding systems (p = 0.777).
relevance_season: Orotic acid concentrations were significantly influenced by season (p = 0.001), with higher concentrations in summer, followed by spring and autumn, and lower in winter.

role: Aromatic essential amino acid and precursor of tyrosine.
biochem: Phenylalanine is a critical substrate for casein synthesis and it is a precursor for tyrosine.
relevance_season: Phenylalanine did not vary significantly across seasons (p = 0.531).

role: Amino acid that is especially abundant in casein.
biochem: Proline is used for the production of β-casein.
relevance_season: Proline concentrations were significantly influenced by season (p < 0.001), with higher concentrations in winter compared to other seasons.

role: Short-chain fatty acid from the rumen and the main glucose precursor in ruminants.
biochem: Propionate is an end product of ruminal fermentation. Propionate is converted into succinyl-CoA, an intermediate of tricarboxylic acid (TCA) cycle, contributing to energy production.
relevance_diet: Propionate concentrations were significantly influenced by feeding systems (p < 0.001), with milk from TMR diets having higher concentrations, followed by PMR diets, and with GRS diets having the lowest concentrations. In the partial least squares discriminant analysis (PLS-DA), propionate exhibited a variable importance in projection (VIP) score higher than 2.0 and in the biomarker analysis comparing GRS vs. TMR, it had an area under the curve (AUC) of 0.95, indicating excellent discriminatory power.

role: End product of glycolysis and entry point to the TCA cycle.
biochem: Pyruvate is a key intermediate in the carbohydrate metabolism and is the end product of glycolysis. Pyruvate can be converted into lactate, acetyl-CoA, oxaloacetate, or alanine, and it serves as a substrate for gluconeogenesis to generate glucose.
relevance_diet: Pyruvate concentrations were significantly influenced by feeding system (p < 0.001), with milk from PMR and TMR diets having higher concentrations compared to GRS.
relevance_season: Pyruvate did not differ significantly across seasons (p = 0.078).

role: TCA cycle intermediate that is also produced by rumen microbes.
biochem: Intermediate in the tricarboxylic acid (TCA) cycle. Succinate is formed from succinyl-CoA and is oxidized to fumarate.
relevance_diet: Succinate concentrations were significantly influenced by feeding systems (p < 0.001), with higher concentrations in milk from PMR and TMR diets compared to GRS diets. In the partial least squares discriminant analysis (PLS-DA), succinate exhibited a variable importance in projection (VIP) score higher than 1.5, with elevated concentrations associated with PMR diets.
relevance_season: Succinate did not vary significantly between seasons (p = 0.311).

role: Microbial product of choline breakdown; at high levels it gives milk a fishy taint.
biochem: Trimethylamine is generated in the rumen from the degradation of dietary quaternary-ammonium compounds.
relevance_season: Trimethylamine concentrations were significantly influenced by season (p < 0.001), with higher concentrations in winter compared to the rest of the seasons.

role: Aromatic amino acid formed from phenylalanine.
biochem: Tyrosine is involved in protein synthesis and is a precursor for catecholamines, melanin, and thyroid hormones. During catabolism, tyrosine is broken down into acetoacetate and fumarate, which feeds into the tricarboxylic acid (TCA) cycle and supports energy production.
relevance_diet: Tyrosine concentrations were not significantly influenced by feeding systems (p = 0.628).

role: End product of protein metabolism; milk urea is used to judge how well dietary protein is used.
biochem: Urea is the principal end product of protein and nitrogen metabolism in mammals. Urea is formed in the liver through urea cycle from ammonia and carbon dioxide and can be diffused into milk from plasma.
relevance_diet: Urea concentrations were not significantly influenced by feeding systems (p = 0.085).
relevance_season: Urea concentrations were significantly influenced by season (p < 0.001), with lower concentrations in winter, followed by spring and summer, and higher in autumn.

role: Pyrimidine nucleoside involved in nucleotide and sugar-nucleotide metabolism.
biochem: Uridine is a key precursor in RNA biosynthesis.
relevance_diet: Uridine concentrations were not significantly influenced by feeding systems (p = 0.284).

role: Short-chain fatty acid from rumen fermentation.
biochem: Valerate is produced by microbial fermentation in the rumen.
relevance_diet: Valerate concentrations were significantly influenced by feeding systems (p = 0.014), with concentrations in PMR diets higher than GRS and TMR.
relevance_season: Valerate did not differ significantly across seasons (p = 0.122).

role: Branched-chain essential amino acid.
biochem: Valine plays a crucial role in protein synthesis and volatile fatty acids like isobutyrate and valerate.
relevance_diet: Valine concentrations were significantly influenced by feeding systems (p < 0.001), with higher concentrations in milk from TMR diets, followed by PMR diets, and with GRS diets having the lowest concentrations. In the partial least squares discriminant analysis (PLS-DA), valine exhibited a variable importance in projection (VIP) score higher than 1.5 and in the biomarker analysis comparing GRS vs. TMR, it had an area under the curve (AUC) of 0.89, indicating good discriminatory power.
relevance_season: Valine did not vary significantly between seasons (p = 0.421).

role: Choline-containing breakdown product of phosphatidylcholine and a major choline form in milk.
biochem: Sn-glycero-3-phosphocholine (GPC) arises from the breakdown of phosphatidylcholine and is a reservoir of choline for the phospholipid synthesis, being involved in the membrane synthesis.
relevance_diet: GPC concentrations were significantly influenced by feeding system (p < 0.001). In summer and autumn, milk from TMR diets exhibited higher GPC concentrations than PMR diets, with the lowest concentrations observed in GRS diets. In spring, PMR and TMR diets had lower GPC concentrations compared to GRS diets.
relevance_season: sn-Glycero-3-phosphocholine concentrations were significantly influenced by season, with a slight decrease from winter to autumn (p = 0.048).
